library(tidyverse)

# Load the three files exactly as provided (no edits to the original CSVs)
GSE.covar.raw <-read_csv("~/Desktop/HDS/HSE103/FinalProject/GSE85307_covar-1.csv")

GSE.GE.raw <-read_csv("~/Desktop/HDS/HSE103/FinalProject/GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")

GSE.GN.raw <-read_csv("~/Desktop/HDS/HSE103/FinalProject/GSE85307_geneNames.csv")

## Step 1: Clean the covariate data

```{r}

head(GSE.covar.raw)
#summary(GSE.covar.raw)

# Data Wrangling time! Whoohoo! Seems like there are some extra text in some
# columns. With the help of the trusty mutate function
# we can clean these cells up!
GSE.covar <- GSE.covar.raw %>%
  mutate(
    mat_age_yrs = str_remove_all(mat_age_yrs,"age_years: "),
    preg_preeclampsia = str_remove_all(preg_preeclampsia, "pregnancy_condition: "),
    delivery_gestAge_wks = str_remove_all(delivery_gestAge_wks, "gestation_weeks: "),
    sampleCollection_gestAge_wks = str_remove_all(sampleCollection_gestAge_wks, 
                                                  "blood_draw_at_gestation_week: "),
    batch_Microarray = str_remove_all(batch_Microarray, "microarray_hybridization_date: "),
    mat_BMI = str_remove_all(mat_BMI, "bmi_kg/m2: "),
    mat_vitD = str_remove_all(mat_vitD, "vitamind_25\\(0h\\)_ng/ml_whole_blood_baseline: "),
    mat_asthma = ifelse(str_ends(mat_asthma, "1"), "1", "0"))


# I also noticed all variables are stored as characters, for safe keeping
# I am going to change the ones that look like numeric measure to numeric 
GSE.covar <- GSE.covar %>%
  mutate(across(c(mat_age_yrs, delivery_gestAge_wks, sampleCollection_gestAge_wks,
                  mat_BMI, mat_vitD),
                as.numeric))


head(GSE.covar)
dim(GSE.covar)
```


## Step 2: Make the categorical variables

```{r}
# Categorical variable #1: preclampsia status (already categories, so we just
# tell R it's a factor and put "Normal" first so it is the reference group).
# Categorical variable #2: vitamin D status, DERIVED from the continuous
# mat_vitD column. Under 20 ng/mL is a commonly used cutoff for deficiency.

GSE.covar <- GSE.covar %>%
  mutate(
    preg_preeclampsia = factor(preg_preeclampsia,
                               levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")),
    vitD_status = factor(ifelse(mat_vitD < 20,
                                "Deficient (<20 ng/mL)",
                                "Sufficient (>=20 ng/mL)"),
                         levels = c("Deficient (<20 ng/mL)",
                                    "Sufficient (>=20 ng/mL)")))


# Check that the new variable makes sense: group sizes, and that the cutoff
# really split the vitamin D values where we said it would.
table(GSE.covar$preg_preeclampsia, GSE.covar$vitD_status)
GSE.covar %>% group_by(vitD_status) %>% summarise(min = min(mat_vitD), max = max(mat_vitD))

```

## Step 3: Clean the gene expression data and attach gene names

```{r}
# The first column of the expression file has a blank header, so we name it
# PROBEID. Probe IDs are just labels, so we store them as text in both tables
# so that R can match them up.

GSE.GE <- GSE.GE.raw %>%
  rename(PROBEID = 1) %>%
  mutate(PROBEID = as.character(PROBEID))

GSE.GN <- GSE.GN.raw %>%
  mutate(PROBEID = as.character(PROBEID))

# Step A: look up the gene name for each probe 
# Step B: pivot_longer turns the sideways table (one column per person) into a
#         tall table with one row per gene per person.

GSE.GE <- GSE.GE %>%
  left_join(GSE.GN, by = "PROBEID") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(PROBEID, GENE),
               names_to = "geoID",
               values_to = "expression")



# Safety checks: every probe got a gene name, and the sample IDs in the
# expression data are exactly the sample IDs in the covariate data.

sum(is.na(GSE.GE$GENE))                              # should be 0
setequal(unique(GSE.GE$geoID), GSE.covar$geoID)      # should be TRUE


head(GSE.GE)

```

## Step 4: Pick our genes and build the plotting table

```{r}

# Not every gene in the linker file is in the expression data, so check first!
genes_of_interest <- c("RUNDC3A", "LYN", "IGFBP1")
genes_of_interest %in% GSE.GE$GENE                   # should be TRUE TRUE TRUE


# Each gene should have exactly 157 rows (one probe, one row per person)
GSE.GE %>% filter(GENE %in% genes_of_interest) %>% count(GENE)

# Keep just our genes, then attach each person's covariates using geoID
dat_all <- GSE.GE %>%
  filter(GENE %in% genes_of_interest) %>%
  left_join(GSE.covar, by = "geoID")

nrow(dat_all)                                        # should be 471
```

## Step 5: Build the plotting function

```{r}

# Inputs:
#   data  = long data frame with one row per person per gene. It needs the
#           columns GENE, expression, mat_BMI, preg_preeclampsia, and vitD_status
#   genes = character vector with the names of 1 or more genes
# Output: prints 3 plots per gene and (invisibly) returns them in a list,
#         so they can be saved for the report late

plot_gene_expression <- function(data, genes) {
  plots <- list()       # holds every plot so we can reuse them later

  
  # Loop through each gene and make its 3 plots
  for (g in genes){
    
    # Keep only this gene's rows
    d <- data %>% filter(GENE == g)

    # Axis label with the gene name in italics (gene names are italicized by convention)
   gene_lab <- bquote(italic(.(g)) ~ "expression level")
    
   
# PLOT 1: Histogram of gene expression
    m <- mean(d$expression); s <- sd(d$expression)
    
    p1 <- ggplot(d, aes(x = expression)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "dodgerblue", color = "white") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = m, color = "orange", linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
      annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.5, size = 5, 
               label = paste0("n = ", nrow(d),
                          "\nMean = ", round(m,2),
                          "\nSD = ", round(s, 2))) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.4))) +
      labs(x = gene_lab,
            y = "Number of samples") +
      theme_classic(base_size = 14)
    
# PLOT 2: Scatterplot of BMI vs. Gener expression
    
    # Pearson correlation between BMI and expression for this gene
    ct <- cor.test (d$mat_BMI, d$expression)
    
    # Write very small p-values as "p < 0.001" so they don't up as "p = 0.00"
    p_text <- ifelse(ct$p.value < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.2f", ct$p.value))
    
    
    p2 <- ggplot(d, aes(x = mat_BMI, y = expression)) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2, color = "dodgerblue") +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y~ x, color = "orange", 
                  fill = "orange", alpha = 0.2) +
     annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 5,
         label = paste0("r = ", round(ct$estimate, 2),
                        "\n", p_text,
                        "\nn = ", sum(!is.na(d$mat_BMI)))) + 
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.4))) +
      labs(x = expression("Maternal BMI (kg/m"^2*")"),
           y = gene_lab) +
      theme_classic(base_size = 14)
    
    
## PLOT 3: Boxplot of expression by both categorical variables
    
    # Group sizes, with the height for the "n = ..." labels set just above this
    # gene's highest point (the old fixed height of 11.4 only worked for one gene)
    n_labels <- d %>%
      count(preg_preeclampsia, vitD_status) %>%
      mutate(y = max(d$expression) + 0.05 * diff(range(d$expression)))
    
    
     p3 <- ggplot(d, aes(x = preg_preeclampsia, y = expression, fill = vitD_status)) +
      geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7,
                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
      geom_point(aes(group = vitD_status),
                 position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15,
                                                 dodge.width = 0.8, seed = 1),
                 alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
      geom_text(data = n_labels, aes(y = y, label = paste0("n = ", n)),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), size = 4) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("orange", "dodgerblue")) +
      labs(x = "Pregnancy outcome",
           y = gene_lab,
           fill = "Vitamin D status") +
      theme_classic(base_size = 14)

# Show the 3 plots (plots made inside a loop don't show up unless we print them)
    print(p1); print(p2); print(p3)

    
    plots[[g]] <- list(histogram = p1, scatter = p2, boxplot = p3)
  }
  invisible(plots)
}
```



```{r}
gene_results <- plot_gene_expression(dat_all, genes_of_interest)
```

Step 7: Summary Statistics table (stratified by preeclampsia)
```{r}
# The table needs 3 contiuous + 2 categorical covariates, stratified by a 
# categorical covariate. We stratify by pregnancy outcome (categorical #1) 
# and show:

# Continuous: maternal BMI (from our plots), maternal age, and gestational
# age at delivery (the 2 new continuous covariates)

# Categorical: vit D status (categorical #2, shown as n (%))
# Continuous variables are summarised as mean (SD) and compared with a 
# Welch two-sample t-test. Vit D status is compared with a chi-squared test

# a Smalle helper: "mean (SD)" text for one numeric vector
mean_sd <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(x), sd(x))

# another small helper: format p-values the same way as the plots
fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p <0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.2f", p))

# The continuous covaraites and the labels we want printed in the table
cont_vars <- c(mat_BMI = "Maternal BMI (kg/m$^2$)",
               mat_age_yrs = "Maternal age (years)",
               delivery_gestAge_wks = "Gestational age at delivery (weeks)")

# One row per continuous covariate: overall, Normal, Preeclampsia, p-value
cont_rows <- map_dfr(names(cont_vars), function(v){
  x <- GSE.covar[[v]]
  grp <- GSE.covar$preg_preeclampsia
  tibble(
    Characteristic = cont_vars[[v]],
    Overall = mean_sd(x),
    Normal = mean_sd(x[grp == "Normal"]),
    Preeclampsia = mean_sd(x[grp == "Preeclampsia"]),
    P = fmt_p(t.test(x ~ grp)$p.value))

})


# Vitamin D status: count and column percent within each pregnancy outcome
vitD_tab <- table(GSE.covar$vitD_status, GSE.covar$preg_preeclampsia)
n_pct <- function(n, total) sprintf("%d (%.1f)", n, 100 * n / total)

cat_rows <- tibble(
  Characteristic = c("Vitamin D status, n (\\%)",
                     "\\quad Deficient ($<$20 ng/mL)",
                     "\\quad Sufficient ($\\geq$20 ng/mL)"),
  Overall = c("", n_pct(rowSums(vitD_tab), nrow(GSE.covar))),
  Normal = c("", n_pct(vitD_tab[, "Normal"], sum(vitD_tab[, "Normal"]))),
  Preeclampsia = c("", n_pct(vitD_tab[, "Preeclampsia"], sum(vitD_tab[, "Preeclampsia"]))),
  P = c(fmt_p(chisq.test(vitD_tab)$p.value), "", ""))


# Stack the rows, then add the group sizes to the column names
table1 <- bind_rows(cont_rows, cat_rows)
n_grp <- table(GSE.covar$preg_preeclampsia)
colnames(table1) <- c("Characteristic",
                      sprintf("Overall (n = %d)", nrow(GSE.covar)),
                      sprintf("Normal (n = %d)", n_grp[["Normal"]]),
                      sprintf("Preeclampsia (n = %d)", n_grp[["Preeclampsia"]]),
                      "$p$-value")


# Write the LaTex version ( just the tabular; the report adds teh caption).
# escape = F so our LaTex symbols ($^2$, \quad, \%) are kept as LaTex. 

table1_tex <- kable(table1, format = "latex", booktabs = T, linesep = "",
                    escape = F, align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c"))
writeLines(table1_tex, "tables/table1.tex")


# Also show it here in the knitted PDF
kable(table1, format = "latex", booktabs = T, escape = F, linesep = "",
      align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c"),
      caption = "Participant characteristics by pregnancy outcome") %>% 
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_positions", "scale_down"))


```

Step 9: Heatmap of the 10 most variable genes

```{r}

# Which 10 genes? We pick the 10 genes whose expression varies the most across
# the 157 women (largest standard deviation). This choice does not use 
# preeclampsia or Vit D at all, so the clustering is not "rigged"
# to seperate the groups

top10 <- GSE.GE %>% 
  group_by(GENE) %>% 
  summarise(sd = sd(expression)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(sd)) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 10)
top10


# pheatmap nees a matrix: one row per gene, one column per women
heat_mat <- GSE.GE %>% 
  filter(GENE %in% top10$GENE) %>% 
  select(GENE, geoID, expression) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = geoID, values_from = expression) %>% 
  column_to_rownames("GENE") %>% 
  as.matrix()

# Tracking bars: one row per woman, named by geoID so pheatmap can line them 
# up with the matrix columns
annot <- GSE.covar %>% 
  select(geoID, preg_preeclampsia, vitD_status) %>% 
  rename(`Pregnancy outcome` = preg_preeclampsia, 
         `Vitamin D status` = vitD_status) %>% 
  column_to_rownames("geoID")
annot <- annot[colnames(heat_mat), ]  # same order as the matrix colimns fyi

# Tracking bar colors (vit D matches teh boxplots: orange / blue)
annot_colors <- list(
  `Pregnancy outcome` = c(Normal = "grey80", Preeclampsia = "black"),
  `Vitamin D status` = c(`Deficient (<20 ng/mL)` = "orange",
                         `Sufficient (>=20 ng/mL)` = "dodgerblue"))


# scale = "row" turns each gene into z-scores, so genes with different
# average levels can share one color scale. Rows(genes) and columns(women)
# are both clustered with Euclidean distance + complete linkage.
heat_args <- list(mat = heat_mat,
                  scale ="row", 
                  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
                  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
                  clustering_method = "complete",
                  annotation_col = annot,
                  annotation_colors = annot_colors,
                                    labels_row = as.expression(lapply(rownames(heat_mat),
                                                    function(x) bquote(italic(.(x))))),
                  color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick"))(100), 
                  show_colnames = F, 
                  treeheight_row = 30, treeheight_col = 40,
                  fontsize =10)



hm <- do.call(pheatmap, heat_args)                       # draws it in the PDF
do.call(pheatmap, c(heat_args, list(filename = "figures/heatmap.pdf", width = 9, height = 5)))

col_clusters <- cutree(hm$tree_col, k = 2)
clust_tab <- table(cluster = col_clusters, outcome = annot[names(col_clusters), "Pregnancy outcome"])
clust_tab
chisq.test(clust_tab)$p.value

```




Step 10: Additional plot: forestplot of adjusted effects
```{r}
# New plot type is ... A forest plot!(aka coefficient plot)
# Instead of looking at one covariate at a time, we fit ONE model per gene. with all three covariates:
#     expression (z-score) ~ preeclampsia + Vit D status + BMI (z-score)
# Expression and BMI are standardised, so every effect is in "SDs of gene 
# expression", which lets us compare the 3 genes on the same axis.
# Dot = estimates, bars = 95% CI, dashed line = no effect.

forest_df <- map_dfr(genes_of_interest, function(g){
  d <- dat_all %>% 
    filter(GENE == g) %>% 
    mutate(expr_z = as.numeric(scale(expression)),
           bmi_z = as.numeric(scale(mat_BMI)))
  fit <- lm(expr_z ~ preg_preeclampsia + vitD_status + bmi_z, data = d)
  ci <- confint(fit)
  tibble(gene = g, 
         term = rownames(ci)[-1],
         estimate = coef(fit)[-1],
         lower = ci[-1,1],
         upper= ci[-1,2],
         p = summary(fit)$coefficients[-1, "Pr(>|t|)"])
}) %>%
  mutate(
    # Give the model terms readable labels for the facet titles
    term = recode(term,
                  preg_preeclampsiaPreeclampsia = "Preeclampsia\n(vs. normal)",
                  `vitD_statusSufficient (>=20 ng/mL)` = "Vitamin D sufficient\n(vs. deficient)",
                  bmi_z = "Maternal BMI\n(per 1 SD)"),
    term = factor(term, levels = c("Preeclampsia\n(vs. normal)",
                                   "Vitamin D sufficient\n(vs. deficient)",
                                   "Maternal BMI\n(per 1 SD)")),
    gene = factor(gene, levels = rev(genes_of_interest)),   # RUNDC3A on top
    significant = ifelse(p < 0.05, "p < 0.05", "p >= 0.05"))

# The numbers behind the forest plot (used in the Results section)
forest_df %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
         
         
         
p_forest <- ggplot(forest_df, aes(x = estimate, y = gene, color = significant)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8, orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ term, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("p < 0.05" = "orange", "p >= 0.05" = "dodgerblue")) +
  labs(x = "Adjusted effect on expression (SD units, 95% CI)",
       y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "lines"))

p_forest

ggsave("figures/forest.pdf", p_forest, width = 9, height = 4)
```
